Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Saturday is a light-wind, stable day under high pressure. Thermals are weak and shallow: thermal strength (w*) mostly 100–240 feet per minute (ft/min), with the thermal top (PBLH) only about 450–1,400 ft above ground level (AGL), and air cooling slowly with height (lapse rate 5.6 °C/km), which means soft, gentle thermals rather than punchy ones. The best options are Rainbow Ridge (east wind plus thermals from 9am) and McClellan (south-southeast flow from late morning to mid-afternoon); NWS Reno also expects light winds and a modest day, with a soaring index of 255 ft/min and a maximum altitude of 8,500 ft above sea level (MSL).

Site Breakdown

McClellan Favorable — Launch-aligned south-southeast wind at 5–7 mph with the area's steadier thermals for about four hours.
Window: 11am–3pm
Thermal strength is 168–211 ft/min from 11am to 2pm, peaking at about 210 ft/min at noon to 1pm, with the thermal top about 520–740 ft AGL. Wind is 5–7 mph from 128°–161°, well within the launch range. Expect light lift rather than big climbs. Watch for a 35° direction change near 936 ft AGL, just above the thermal top.
Rainbow Ridge Favorable — Steady east-northeast wind on launch all day with positive ridge lift and the strongest thermals of the area.
Window: 9am–3pm
Thermal strength is 167–240 ft/min from 9am to 2pm, peaking at 240 ft/min at noon, with the thermal top about 850–1,080 ft AGL. Wind is 5–9 mph from 63°–101°. Ridge lift is +134 ft/min early, easing to +79 ft/min by 2pm, which helps but is not enough on its own to stay up. Expect a sharp 67° direction change near 929 ft AGL, close to the thermal top, so be ready for bumpy air there.

Not recommended today (7) — click a row for details

Kingsbury grade Marginal — Near-calm, variable wind and weak, very shallow thermals make this mostly a sled ride.
Window: 10:30am–1:30pm
Thermal strength peaks at 110–140 ft/min from 10am to 1pm, with the thermal top only about 370–470 ft above launch. Wind is 1–2 miles per hour (mph) and wanders through east to northeast (153° to 55°), so it is fine for a no-wind launch but gives no ridge lift (calm all day). The thermal onset of 10:00 is new in this run; the previous run had none.
Hallelujah Marginal — Thermals are workable, but the wind only lines up with launch for a few hours and is light.
Window: 12:30pm–3pm
Thermal strength is 195–212 ft/min from noon to 2pm, with the thermal top about 1,050 ft AGL around 1–2pm. Wind turns from north-northwest (off launch) at midday to west-southwest at 4–5 mph around 1–2pm (248°–225°), then drifts south of the preferred range by 3pm. Ridge lift of about +100 ft/min is overstated because stable air flows around most of the slope below launch. The direction change near 580 ft AGL is 33° per 100 m.
West McClellan Marginal — Wind is south of the launch direction until about 2pm, leaving a short aligned window.
Window: 1:30pm–3pm
Thermal strength is 161–179 ft/min from 1–2pm and drops to 104 ft/min by 3pm, with the thermal top about 830–850 ft AGL. Wind comes onto launch at only 3 mph from 250° at 2pm and 240° at 3pm. Earlier it is from the south-southeast (off launch, negative ridge lift), and by 4pm it backs to 207°.
Peavine Mountain Marginal — Only a morning sled ride has launch-aligned wind; from late morning the 12–14 mph west-southwest wind is crossed and the slope sinks.
Window: 9am–10:30am
From 8–10am, wind is 10–11 mph from 180°–194° (on launch), but thermal strength is only 29–67 ft/min, so plan a sled ride. From 11am the wind is from 230°–240° at 8–14 mph, outside the launch range, with negative ridge lift (-40 to -83 ft/min), even though thermals reach about 200 ft/min and the thermal top reaches about 1,000–1,130 ft AGL. The peak 10 m wind is 18 mph, and the direction change near 572 ft AGL is 34° per 100 m.
Daydreams Marginal — Wind is nearly calm and thermals are weak, so expect mostly a sled ride with short scratchy climbs.
Window: 12pm–4:20pm
Thermal strength is only 71–105 ft/min all day (105 at 9am, about 80 at midday), with the thermal top about 420–540 ft AGL. Wind is 1–3 mph and lines up with launch from noon (200°–248°). At 4pm, ridge lift of +109 ft/min on 3 mph from 230° may give a gentle late-day float, but it is not enough to soar on. Peak wind dropped from 13 to 7 mph since the previous run.
Slide Mountain Unfavorable — West wind puts the south-facing launch in the lee from midday, with strong sink on the slope.
Thermals are weak, with thermal strength peaking at 141 ft/min at noon and the thermal top about 530 ft AGL. Morning wind is from the south-southwest at 5–7 mph, just outside the launch range. From 1pm the wind turns west at 6–12 mph, and ridge lift is negative all day, reaching -321 to -386 ft/min from 2–4pm (launch on the downwind side). Peak thermal strength rose from 57 to 158 ft/min since the previous run, but it is still too weak to offset the lee position.
Duck Hill Unfavorable — Wind is from the south-southeast all day, directly behind the west-to-north-facing launch.
Wind blows 8–11 mph from 145°–156° all day, including late afternoon, so there is no evening window either. Ridge lift is negative at every hour. Thermals reach about 190 ft/min at noon, but launch conditions rule the site out.

Hazards

  • Low-level wind shear: Sharp direction changes near the thermal tops are forecast at several sites: Rainbow Ridge 67° and Duck Hill 57° per 100 m, McClellan 35°, Peavine 34° and Hallelujah 33°, mostly 570–940 ft AGL. Speed-and-direction shear also reaches 5–8 mph per 100 m at most sites, so expect bumpy transitions when climbing out of the lowest layer.
  • Lee-side sink at Slide and Peavine: From midday, west to west-southwest surface wind puts Slide Mountain's launch on the downwind side, with ridge lift of -321 to -386 ft/min from 2–4pm. Peavine shows sink of -40 to -83 ft/min from 11am to 4pm. Stay out of the lee of the Carson Range and Peavine ridgelines, where rotor is possible.
  • Weak, shallow thermals: Thermals are close to paraglider sink rate at most sites, and NWS Reno's trigger temperature of 67 °F equals its forecast high, so climbs may be hard to start. Plan for sled rides and keep landing options in reach.
  • Crest-level wind and wave: Wind near Sierra crest height (700 hPa) is only 3–10 knots on Saturday, far below the roughly 25 knots that brings wave and downslope winds, so that risk is low today. NWS Reno expects stronger winds around 10,000 ft MSL with brief low-level wind shear and mountain wave turbulence starting early Sunday, not Saturday.
  • Morning haze and cloud uncertainty: NWS Reno mentions valley inversions and morning haze reducing slant visibility near Reno airport, with no timing beyond mornings. WRF now shows about 35–48% average cloud cover at most sites, up from 10–24% in the previous run, while NWS terminal forecasts show only clear skies or a few high clouds. Cloud bases are well above the thermal tops, so cloud suck is not a concern.
